question: In general, the oxides of non-metals are ________ in nature.
solution:
The correct answer is **' Acidic'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **Oxides of Non-Metals are **acidic** in nature.
 
• When a Non-Metal reacts with Oxygen, it gives **Oxide **which on **dissolution with wate**r gives an **acid.**
 
• Such a molecule readily loses a proton from one of its hydroxyl groups because the resulting anion is highly stabilized by the oxygen atoms and the electronegative non-metal atom. Therefore, they are **acidic.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information __**

 
• **Most non-metal oxides are acidic, but not all**. For example, **carbon monoxide** (CO) is not** acidic.**
 
• **neutral:**
 
 
• **​**With a pH of **7**, neutral substances don't change color when exposed to any **indicator**.
 
• Nature is neutral in **pure water**.
 
 
 
• **basic:**
 
 
• ​Any material that is slippery to the touch, **tastes unpleasant**, alters the** color of indicators (such as turning red litmus paper blue)**, combines with acids to generate salts, and facilitates certain chemical processes is considered a base in chemistry (base catalysis).
 
 
 
• **amphoteric:**
 
 
• **​**Amphoteric refers to **both an acid and a base.**
 
• Amphoteric oxides exhibit both basic and acidic characteristics. Examples are the **oxides of zinc and aluminium**.
